conventions.convention: A framing is an actual smooth trivialization of the quotient normal bundle TX|N/TN, not merely stable triviality. Rank-zero and empty framings are unique. Countable Choice is inherited from the normal-bundle supplier.

Framed cobordisms are compact neat embedded submanifolds of X×[0,1] with literal product ends and framings equal to the supplied end framings throughout their collars; there is no additional inward-normal sign.

The collapse is based at the disjoint point of X+, and its restriction to X need not preserve a preselected basepoint. The normalized smooth representative has target coordinate exactly equal to the framed normal coordinate near its centre.

Regular-preimage framings use the normal differential followed by the coordinate isomorphism of a positively oriented target basis. Regular-value independence and the fixed-codimension correspondence require k≥1.

The stabilization system starts at codimension k=1, preserves the submanifold dimension, and prepends the chosen outward equatorial normal. Addition uses separately packed representatives, rather than unions of arbitrary embeddings.

Handle chains are right Z[π]-modules with c·g=T(g⁻¹)c. Differential matrices have lower handles as rows and upper handles as columns, and act on coordinate columns on the left. Integral coefficients in universal-cover cellular homology are not replaced by a second group-ring coefficient system.

Torsion is indexed by the finite presentation H. For differential A in degrees q+1,q, τ_H=(-1)^q[A], using odd-to-even contraction torsion. Invariance is supplied for fixed auxiliary choices and the listed elementary moves, not asserted for arbitrary presentations.

The product criterion concerns nonempty connected oriented h-cobordisms with boundary dimension n≥5 and says product iff some finite presentation has zero torsion. The realization and universal-cover Hurewicz route explicitly assume full AC.

Leafwise paths and homotopies are initially continuous into the ambient manifold. Under Countable Choice, the provided countable-plaque argument identifies interval and square maps with maps into the intrinsic leaf topology.

Fundamental-group products traverse the first loop first, while germ multiplication is ordinary composition. Forward transport satisfies h(a*b)=h_b∘h_a; the homomorphic holonomy representation is ρ([a])=h_(a⁻¹).
Pullback leaves are connected components of N×M L with the intrinsic fibre-product manifold topology, which need not equal the subspace topology of f⁻¹(L) in N.

Proper discontinuity means finitely many translates meet any given compact set. The suspension uses the diagonal left action (γx,ρ(γ)y), so forward transport over γ is the germ of ρ(γ)⁻¹; the leaf representation on its stabilizer uses ρ(γ).

Monodromy and holonomy groupoids are defined set-theoretically here, without arrow-space topology. The separate non-Hausdorff remark records an external result; its stated independence is supported by Meinrenken Remark 2.10 and Exercises 2.3–2.4, checked at https://www.math.toronto.edu/mein/teaching/MAT1341_LieGroupoids/Groupoids.pdf.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice, X closed and smooth, and k≥1. If f:X→S^k is smooth, y is regular and b is a positive basis at y, the Pontryagin–Thom map of (f⁻¹(y),f_*b) is smoothly homotopic to f. The same collapse-class conclusion holds under continuous homotopy when f is continuous and smooth near its regular fibre.

Under Countable Choice, for closed smooth X and k≥0, framed cobordism consists of a compact neat embedded codimension-k W⊂X×I with the specified boundary, literal product ends of width ε∈(0,1/2), and a normal framing equal to the pullback of each supplied end framing throughout its collar.

Assume Countable Choice. For n≥k≥1, collapse and framed regular preimage define mutually inverse bijections between framed cobordism classes of closed framed (n-k)-submanifolds of S^n and π_n(S^k), equivalently [S^n,S^k]. Empty preimages and n=k are included.

Assume Countable Choice. Every nonempty connected oriented compact smooth h-cobordism of dimension n+1≥6, with closed connected oriented boundary n-manifolds, admits for every 2≤q≤n-2 a relative presentation with only q- and (q+1)-handles, related by the listed elementary modifications. The two handle numbers agree and its right-module differential matrix is invertible; simple connectivity is not assumed.

Assume Countable Choice. For a nonempty connected compact smooth (n+1)-manifold, n+1≥6, with all relative handle indices at least q, 2≤q≤n-3, an embedded q-sphere whose ambient-cover handle class is one basis class times ±γ is isotopic in the q-level to meet that handle's belt once and every other belt not at all. At q=2 additionally assume incoming π₁ injects into the trace through the 2-handles.

Assume Countable Choice. A nonempty connected smooth h-cobordism of dimension n+1≥6 with a two-index presentation in q,q+1, 2≤q≤n-2, having equal handle numbers and diagonal intersection matrix diag(±g_i), admits attaching isotopies giving exactly one intersection per matching pair and none elsewhere. Cancelling all pairs gives the product relative to M₀.

Assume Countable Choice. For a nonempty connected h-cobordism with a finite relative handle decomposition, its based handle complex over Z[π₁(M₀)] admits a right-linear contraction ds+sd=id, constructed from lifted homotopy-equivalence data rather than inferred merely from acyclicity.

Assume AC. For every nonempty closed connected oriented smooth n-manifold M, n≥5, π=π₁(M), and u∈Wh(π), there exists an (n+1)-dimensional h-cobordism over M with a relative 2/3-handle presentation and invertible differential A having [A]=τ_H=u. The construction realizes any prescribed invertible matrix representing u.

Under Countable Choice, for a leaf L, x∈L and local transversal T, the holonomy representation is the homomorphism ρ_x:π₁(L,x)→Diff_x(T), ρ_x([a])=h_(a⁻¹)(T,T). Its image is the leaf holonomy group. Changing T conjugates the representation and leaves its kernel unchanged.

Assume Countable Choice. For a regular foliation, leafwise paths a,b from x to y that are leafwise homotopic relative to endpoints have equal holonomy germs between any fixed local endpoint transversals.

Assume Countable Choice. A group acting freely and properly discontinuously by diffeomorphisms on a smooth manifold, preserving a regular foliation, has a unique smooth quotient making the orbit map a covering and local diffeomorphism. The quotient foliation has leaves equal to images of the original leaves, unchanged codimension, and tangent distribution dπ(TF).

Assume Countable Choice. In the specified diagonal suspension, a lifted base loop γ gives forward holonomy germ germ_y(ρ([γ])⁻¹). The leaf through y is diffeomorphic to the universal base cover modulo K_y={γ:ρ(γ)y=y}; its fundamental group identifies with K_y and its homomorphic leaf representation is γ↦germ_y(ρ(γ)).

concerns.concern: The Statement calls the sphere-valued map the composite of c:X+→Th(ν) with the projection N+∧S^k→S^k, omitting the intervening framing homeomorphism Φ_φ. Those two displayed maps are not directly composable. Proof Step 3.1 correctly gives p∘Φ_φ∘c; make the Statement equally explicit.

Fact F3 says 'no equality of classes from different presentations is asserted anywhere'. The cited elementary-move invariance lemma explicitly asserts τ_H=τ_H′ for different presentations related by the listed moves. The intended caveat is absence of invariance under arbitrary presentation changes, as the Statement correctly says.

alerts.finding: In this C²-foliation item, F2 says 'Holonomy germs of leafwise paths between fixed endpoint transversals depend only on the leafwise homotopy class relative to endpoints' and cites thm-holonomy-depends-only-on-leafwise-homotopy-relative-endpoints and the smooth holonomy representation Definition. Those suppliers concern smooth regular foliations and smooth diffeomorphism germs. The consumer already opens the correct regularity bridge through F3, lem-c2-plaque-transport-and-transverse-fences-preserve-c2-regularity, whose clause (c) supplies C² holonomy well-definedness and homotopy invariance. The conclusion has available support, but F2's direct supplier attribution changes the regularity domain.

For the stated C² foliation, F3 says 'Identity holonomy of a leafwise-null frontier follows from' def-holonomy-representation-and-holonomy-group-of-a-leaf and thm-holonomy-depends-only-on-leafwise-homotopy-relative-endpoints. These are smooth-foliation suppliers. The C² analogue is available in lem-c2-plaque-transport-and-transverse-fences-preserve-c2-regularity, clause (c), and its C¹ prerequisite, both opened. The smooth-only citation should identify that bridge rather than silently broadening the cited domain.

seams_checked.note: Checked the h-cobordism Definition, finite relative CW and handle-complex interfaces, framed trading hypotheses, belt-complement injection, complementary indices and empty-presentation product conclusion. The group-ring extension is derived locally; the arbitrary-sphere homology lemma is restricted to q≤n-3 and the flipped endpoint uses actual reversed handle belts.

The concrete use is the orientation-double-cover lemma in ex-simply-connected-h-cobordisms-have-zero-whitehead-obstruction, F6. Its nonempty connected and boundaryless hypotheses are met for M₀ and for int(W); collar extension to W is explained locally.

Reversed-loop multiplication is preserved, including the one-sided kernel and normal-subgroup arguments. Some C² cap consumers directly cite the smooth-only holonomy theorem and Definition for homotopy invariance. The opened C² plaque-transport supplier supplies the needed extension, but the direct regularity attribution needs correction; routed alert identifies a concrete consumer.

The page lists this prerequisite but its current items have no direct citation or dependency on an owned framed item. Its universal Thom-prespectrum correspondence is presented separately, without claiming that the fixed-codimension sphere theorem proves unoriented or oriented universal bordism.

The holonomy-cover deck lemma explicitly uses ρ([a])=h_(a⁻¹), and transverse transport retains fixed endpoint transversals and germ-level equality. Finite diagonal actions meet the quotient supplier's properness hypothesis. The solid-torus item explicitly extends across its boundary before applying the boundaryless quotient theorem.

The concrete current citation is cex-a-homology-cobordism-need-not-be-an-h-cobordism, F3, using smooth path connectivity of positive bases. It states that supplier faithfully and does not assert a framed Pontryagin–Thom classification of homology cobordisms.

Checked normal trivializations versus inverse frame-bundle frames, literal product collars, disjointness of whole cobordism images, positive target bases, k=m≥1, regular-value independence and the two inverse collapse comparisons. General-domain Hopf consumers use the general closed-X lemmas rather than broadening the sphere-domain fixed-codimension theorem.

Transversality and the null-loop identity-germ consequence are used in the correct direction. A C² cancellation consumer directly attributes identity holonomy to smooth-only suppliers; the available C²/C¹ bridge closes the mathematical support but should be the explicit citation. No forward/reversed-loop distinction affects the identity-germ consequence.
